_source: OSRS Wiki: Eagle_transport_system, Polar_eagle, Jungle_eagle, Desert_eagle, Growing_vine; Transcript:Eagles'_Peak for the refusal. Ids are cache gamevals; tiles are from the map (collision checked).
_farEagles: The far eyries' own eagles (1491-1493) are multinpcs the cache shows at eaglepeak_quest 40, a value the Eagles' Peak plugin's stages never reach; a player who has done the quest gets their own Quick-travel eagle (the Peak's ids, which have the option) on each of their tiles instead.
_peak: The Eagles' Peak eyrie (plane 3, past the stone door): eagles in it fly out to the other three.
_eyries: Each eyrie: where a flight from the Peak lands, and its cave in and out. The Peak eagle's shown id picks the eyrie.
_travelTicks: Calibrated: the lasso, then a fade, then the move (no capture of the flight).
_boulder: Wiki: 45 Strength (boosts count) to push the boulder by the desert eyrie's exit. It stands in the one-tile passage between the exit and the eagles; a push takes the player past it either way.
_vine: Wiki Growing_vine: an item stuck in by the young vine guides it; it grows within a couple of minutes, and is climbable after about 40 (the Wiki's figure), with the line below. Varbit eaglepeak_jungle_vine: 1 guided, 2 growing, 3 tall. The growing step is calibrated.

messages.questIncomplete: You must have completed the Eagles' Peak quest before you can try to lasso a giant eagle.
messages.noRope: You need a rope to lasso the eagle.
messages.lasso: You lasso the eagle and it carries you off.
messages.vineGuided: You stick the {item} into the ground beside the young vine.
messages.vineGrown: Those vines should be worth checking on now.
messages.vineNotReady: The vine isn't strong enough to climb yet.
messages.vineAlready: The vine is already being guided.
messages.boulderWeak: You need a Strength level of 45 to push this boulder.
messages.boulderPush: You push the boulder aside and squeeze past.
messages._unverified: questIncomplete is the transcript's; vineGrown is the Wiki's quote. The rest have no capture behind them.
